plain.headline: The Word Became Flesh
plain.intro: On Christmas Day the readings look beyond the manger to who this child is. Isaiah sees a messenger crossing the mountains with news that God has come to save his people, and the Letter to the Hebrews says that God, who once spoke through the prophets, now speaks to us through his Son. John's Gospel tells us that the eternal Word of God, through whom all things were made, became a human being and lived among us.
plain.listen: the Word who was with God from the beginning, and the moment the Word becomes flesh

Reading 1.box: Isaiah pictures a messenger racing over the hills toward Jerusalem with news of peace and salvation, while the city's watchmen shout for joy. These words first gave hope to God's people in exile, longing to go home. On Christmas the Church hears in them the news that God has come to save his people.

chunks.text: How beautiful it is to see a messenger coming over the mountains, bringing good news, announcing peace, bringing joyful news, announcing salvation, and saying to Zion, "Your God is King." Your watchmen raise their voices and sing together, because they will see with their own eyes the Lord coming back to Zion.

Burst into song together, you ruins of Jerusalem, because the Lord has comforted his people. He has set Jerusalem free. The Lord has shown his holy strength in front of all the nations. The whole earth, to its farthest ends, has seen our God save his people.

Responsorial Psalm.box: The psalm calls the whole earth to sing a new song, with harps, trumpets, and horns, because God has worked salvation for everyone to see. It echoes the first reading: all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.

Reading 2.box: The Letter to the Hebrews opens by saying that God, who spoke through the prophets in many ways, has now spoken to us in his own Son. The Son shares God's glory, holds all creation in being, and has taken away our sins, so he stands far above the angels. The writer quotes the psalms and God's promise to David to show who Jesus is.

chunks.text: Long ago, God spoke to our ancestors many times and in many ways through the prophets. But now, in these last days, he has spoken to us through his Son. God made the Son heir of all things, and through him God made the universe.

The Son is the shining light of God's glory and the exact image of who God is. He holds all things together by his powerful word. After he cleansed us from our sins, he sat down at the right hand of God's majesty in heaven. So he is as far above the angels as the name he received is greater than theirs.

God never said to any angel, "You are my Son. Today I have become your Father." Nor did he say of an angel, "I will be his Father, and he will be my Son." And when God brings his firstborn into the world, he says, "Let all of God's angels worship him."

Gospel.box: John begins his Gospel not in Bethlehem but before creation itself. "The Word" is John's name for God's Son: the one in whom God fully expresses himself, who was with God from the beginning and is God, and through whom everything was made. At Christmas this eternal Word became a human being, Jesus, so that we could see God's glory and become God's children.

chunks.text: In the beginning, the Word already was. The Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was with God from the very beginning.

Everything was made through him. Nothing that exists was made without him. In him was life, and that life was the light of all people. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
God sent a man named John. He came as a witness, to tell about the light so that everyone could believe through him. John himself was not the light. He came to point people to the light.

The true light, which gives light to every person, was coming into the world. He was in the world, and the world was made through him, yet the world did not recognize him. He came to his own people, and his own people did not welcome him.
But to all who did welcome him, all who believe in his name, he gave the power to become children of God. They are born not from human blood, or human desire, or a man's choice, but from God.
The Word became flesh, a real human being, and lived among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the Father's only Son, full of grace and truth.

John spoke out about him and cried, "This is the one I told you about when I said, 'The one who comes after me ranks ahead of me, because he existed before me.'" From his fullness we have all received one gift of grace after another.
God gave the Law through Moses. Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. No one has ever seen God. But the only Son, who is closest to the Father's heart, has made him known.

plain.carry: This week I will spend a few quiet minutes with the Christmas story and remember that God did not stay far away, but became one of us.

kids.headline: God Comes to Live With Us
kids.intro: Merry Christmas. Today we celebrate the birthday of Jesus. The readings tell us who this baby really is: God's own Son, who came to live with us.
kids.listen: the word "light" and how many times you hear it

Reading 1.box: Isaiah pictures a messenger running over the mountains with wonderful news: God is coming to save his people. Everyone who hears it starts singing for joy.

chunks.text: How wonderful it is to see a messenger running over the mountains with good news. He calls out, "Peace has come. God is saving us. Your God is King." The watchmen on the city walls sing for joy, because they can see God coming back. Even the broken parts of the city start to sing, because God has comforted his people. God has shown his great power, and the whole world can see him save his people.

Responsorial Psalm.box: This song tells the whole world to sing a new song to God, with harps and trumpets, because God has done amazing things to save us.

Reading 2.box: This letter tells us that long ago God spoke through prophets, but now God speaks to us through his own Son, Jesus. Jesus is greater than all the angels, and even the angels worship him.

chunks.text: Long ago God spoke to people in many ways through the prophets. Now God has spoken to us through his Son. Everything was made through the Son, and everything belongs to him. The Son shines with God's glory and shows us exactly who God is. He keeps the whole world going. He took away our sins, and then he sat down at God's right hand in heaven.
Jesus is much greater than the angels. God never said to an angel, "You are my Son." But God said it to Jesus. And when God sent Jesus into the world, he said, "All of God's angels, worship him."

Gospel.box: Saint John calls Jesus "the Word." Our words let others know what we think and who we are, and Jesus lets us know who God is. Jesus was always with God the Father, and he is God, and at Christmas he became a baby so he could live with us.

chunks.text: Before anything else existed, the Word was there. The Word was with God, and the Word was God. God made everything through the Word. The Word gives life, and that life is a light for everyone. The light shines in the dark, and the dark can never put it out.
God sent a man named John. John's job was to tell people about the light so they would believe. John was not the light. He came to point to the light.

The true light, Jesus, was coming into the world to shine on everyone. He made the world, but the world did not know who he was. Even his own people did not welcome him. But everyone who welcomes him and believes in him becomes a child of God.
The Word became a human being, a real baby, and came to live with us. We have seen his glory. He is God's only Son, full of God's love and truth.

John told everyone, "This is the one I was talking about. He comes after me, but he is greater than me, because he was alive before me." From Jesus we all receive gift after gift. God gave the Law through Moses, but God's love and truth came to us through Jesus. No one has ever seen God, but Jesus, God's only Son, who is closest to the Father's heart, has shown us who God is.

word.meaning: In John's Gospel, "the Word" is a name for Jesus, God's Son, who was with God from the beginning and shows us who God is.

kids.draw: Draw baby Jesus in the manger with bright light shining out from him into a dark night.
kids.ask: Jesus came to be the light for everyone. How can you share his light with someone this Christmas?

family.opener: Today we celebrate that God's Son, who was with God before the world began, was born as a baby to live with us.
questions: John says Jesus is the light that shines in the darkness. Where does our family need his light right now?
Why do you think God chose to come to us as a little baby instead of as a powerful king?
Some people did not welcome Jesus. How can we welcome him in our home this Christmas?
family.try: Each evening this week, light a candle at dinner and read one line from today's Gospel together, starting with "The light shines in the darkness."
family.pray: Jesus, Word of God made flesh, thank you for coming to live among us, and fill our family with your light and love.
